subject: Accounting
title: Tax Havens
description: A fast breakdown of Tax Havens for builders.

hook.text: The Cayman Islands has zero income tax, zero corporate tax, and more registered companies than people.

buildup.text: Tax havens attract money by offering low or no taxes and strict financial secrecy laws.

discovery.text: Companies route profits through havens using legal structures, reducing their global tax bill.

twist.text: An estimated $7.6 trillion in personal wealth is held offshore—escaping taxes in home countries.

climax.text: Global efforts like the OECD's minimum tax aim to close these gaps, but progress is slow.

punchline.text: Where there's a zero tax rate, money follows.

quiz.question: What makes a country a tax haven?
options: Very low taxes and financial secrecy
Free trade agreements with all nations

details.summary: Tax havens are jurisdictions that attract foreign capital by offering very low or zero tax rates, strict banking secrecy, and minimal financial reporting requirements. They enable legal tax avoidance but also facilitate illegal tax evasion.
details.whyItMatters: Tax havens cost governments hundreds of billions in lost revenue annually and sit at the center of global debates about corporate responsibility, wealth inequality, and international tax cooperation.
takeaways: Tax havens attract foreign investment through low taxes, secrecy, and minimal regulation
Multinational corporations use havens to shift profits away from higher-tax countries where they operate
The distinction between legal tax avoidance and illegal tax evasion can be very thin in practice

faq.question: What makes a country a tax haven?
faq.answer: Tax havens typically offer very low or zero corporate and income tax rates, strict banking secrecy laws, minimal financial reporting requirements, and easy company formation. Popular havens include the Cayman Islands, Bermuda, Luxembourg, and Ireland (for corporate tax).

faq.question: Are tax havens legal?
faq.answer: Using tax havens for legal tax planning is lawful, though increasingly scrutinized. The line between legal avoidance and illegal evasion depends on whether income is properly reported. International efforts like CRS (Common Reporting Standard) are making it harder to hide assets offshore.
